audit.why: 51.98% over 756 games. A tank mirror that produces almost no solo kills; the existing framing (Sion edges levels 2-3 off Roar poke and armour shred, Cho'Gath stabilises from 3 onward) matches both the number and the kits.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four stages contradict the page's own whys[]. whys[2] says 'the trades reset to even' but Level 3 is scored Sion; whys[4] says Feast 'is the one tool that actually threatens to execute a tank and deters his all-in' but Level 6 is scored Skill; whys[5] says 'the first-item window stays even' but First item is scored Sion; whys[6] says the two 'can't solo each other' but 2+ items is scored Sion.
audit.why: The packet chart matches the whys row for row. Mechanically: Level 6 is Cho'Gath's alone because Feast's true damage is the only thing in either kit that threatens an armour-stacking tank, while Unstoppable Onslaught (140s at rank 1) adds nothing to a 1v1 he is already in. First item and 2+ items are genuinely even — both stack health, neither can finish the other.
audit.corrected: Level 3 Skill, Level 6 Cho'Gath (6/10), First item Skill, 2+ items Skill. Proposed as one atomic chart group across both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Glory in Death (P) does not appear anywhere on the page. Sion's death is not the end of the fight: he reanimates with rapid attacks that HEAL him and deal bonus damage based on the TARGET'S MAXIMUM HEALTH. Against the one champion in the game whose win condition is an unbounded health pool, that is the decisive interaction and it is entirely absent. Separately, spikes[1] claims Feast's true damage 'bypasses the bonus HP from his Soul Furnace shield' — true damage does not bypass health, and Soul Furnace's detonation is itself max-health scaling, which is the fact that actually matters.
audit.why: Riot text — Glory in Death: 'After being killed, Sion will temporarily reanimate with rapidly decaying Health. His attacks become very rapid, heal him, and deal bonus damage based on his target's maximum Health.' Soul Furnace: shields, reactivates after 3s for magic damage, and permanently gains max health on kills; kit carries the percentHealth flag. Roar of the Slayer: 800 range, reduces ARMOR, and knocks a struck minion back through everything behind it. Decimating Smash: 10/9/8/7/6s, 45 mana, and only knocks up and stuns if charged long enough. Unstoppable Onslaught: 140/100/60s, 7500 range, steerable, knockup scaling with distance charged.
audit.corrected: Glory in Death and its Grievous Wounds requirement added to dontsFull[2], report[5].t and wants.foe[2]; Soul Furnace's max-health detonation replaces the 'bypasses bonus HP' error in spikes[1].text; real cooldowns added to breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns gave no numbers for either Decimating Smash or Unstoppable Onslaught.
audit.why: Decimating Smash is 10s at rank 1 and only stuns fully charged — the wind-up itself is the window. Unstoppable Onslaught is 140s at rank 1, so a dodged or wasted R takes Sion out of the fight for over two minutes.

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal anywhere in the Sion page.
audit.why: The _missing file flags Sion under needs-antiheal specifically because of Glory in Death's heal-on-hit, and Roar of the Slayer's armour shred means Cho'Gath cannot simply out-resist him.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds named in dontsFull[2].d and report[5].t rather than a separate itemisation edit, to keep the change inside the length band.

notes: DERIVED-FLAG MISFIRE: Sion's Unstoppable Onslaught (R) carries a 'terrain: creates terrain, blocks paths and dashes' flag, and champ-data/_kits/_missing/chogath.json repeats it as 'Sion can cut your retreat with Unstoppable Onslaught (R)... hold Flash for the wall.' Riot's own description contains no terrain creation — it is a steerable charge that damages and knocks up on collision. Per the instructions I trusted the description and did NOT write any wall/terrain claim into the page. The _missing entry for sion should be regarded as tainted on that point. Cho'Gath's own Rupture 'grounding' flag is the same class of misfire (Riot says it pops units into the air) and was likewise not used.
